title: Zuriel Names and Titles of God Study Library
description: Contextual reference collection of biblical names, titles and descriptions of God, with original-language forms, Scripture references and interpretive notes.
editorialPolicy: Original-language glosses are concise study aids, not exhaustive lexicon definitions.
Some traditional forms and etymologies are debated; uncertainty is stated where relevant.
Read each title in its literary, historical and covenant context.
Distinguish titles used for God, titles used for Jesus, and poetic descriptions.
References are study starting points; read the full passage.

entries.name: YHWH
entries.senseAndContext: The divine name revealed to Moses; commonly rendered LORD in English Bibles.
entries.studyNote: Study God's self-revelation and deliverance; English traditions differ on vocalisation.

entries.name: Elohim
entries.senseAndContext: A common designation for God, prominent in creation and worship texts.
entries.studyNote: Read its grammatical and literary setting; do not build simplistic claims on form alone.

entries.name: El
entries.senseAndContext: A Semitic word for God, appearing in poetry and compound titles.
entries.studyNote: Context determines the emphasis of this broad designation.

entries.name: Adonai
entries.senseAndContext: Lord or Master; a reverential title expressing divine authority.
entries.studyNote: Notice the response of worship and service.

entries.name: El Elyon
entries.senseAndContext: God Most High; a title highlighting supreme rule.
entries.studyNote: Read first in the story of Melchizedek and Abram.

entries.name: El Shaddai
entries.senseAndContext: Traditionally rendered God Almighty; its precise etymology is debated.
entries.studyNote: Focus on covenant promises; do not present disputed etymology as settled.

entries.name: El Olam
entries.senseAndContext: God Everlasting; associated with God's enduring nature.
entries.studyNote: Consider faithfulness across generations.

entries.name: El Roi
entries.senseAndContext: The God who sees; Hagar's expression after her encounter in the wilderness.
entries.studyNote: Keep Hagar's vulnerability and story central.

entries.name: YHWH Yireh
entries.senseAndContext: The LORD will provide or see to it; associated with Abraham on Moriah.
entries.studyNote: Do not turn this testing narrative into a guarantee of every desired outcome.

entries.name: YHWH Rapha
entries.senseAndContext: The LORD who heals you; spoken after the waters of Marah.
entries.studyNote: Read covenant context and the wider biblical witness about healing.

entries.name: YHWH Nissi
entries.senseAndContext: The LORD is my banner; Moses names an altar after the conflict with Amalek.
entries.studyNote: Notice communal struggle and the memorial altar.

entries.name: YHWH Shalom
entries.senseAndContext: The LORD is peace; Gideon's altar name after a divine encounter.
entries.studyNote: Peace here is more than a pleasant feeling; read Gideon's fear and calling.

entries.name: YHWH Tsidqenu
entries.senseAndContext: The LORD is our righteousness; a title in Jeremiah's promise of a righteous ruler.
entries.studyNote: Read within Jeremiah's hope for just leadership and restoration.

entries.name: YHWH Sabaoth
entries.senseAndContext: The LORD of hosts; stresses God's command over heavenly hosts.
entries.studyNote: The title is not a licence for human aggression.

entries.name: YHWH Shammah
entries.senseAndContext: The LORD is there; the name of the restored city in Ezekiel's vision.
entries.studyNote: The vision culminates in God's presence among His people.

entries.name: YHWH Mekaddishkem
entries.senseAndContext: The LORD who sanctifies you; a covenant declaration.
entries.studyNote: Sanctification is God's work, connected with covenant life.

entries.name: Qanna
entries.senseAndContext: A description of God as jealous, expressing exclusive covenant loyalty.
entries.studyNote: Explain the metaphor within covenant faithfulness and rejection of idolatry.

entries.name: Ehyeh-Asher-Ehyeh
entries.senseAndContext: God's phrase to Moses, rendered I AM WHO I AM or I WILL BE WHAT I WILL BE.
entries.studyNote: Translations reflect interpretive choices; note the promise of God's presence.

entries.name: Ab
entries.senseAndContext: Father; a relational title expressing care, authority and covenant relationship.
entries.studyNote: Read within the specific covenant and communal context.

entries.name: Goel
entries.senseAndContext: Redeemer or kinsman-redeemer; one who rescues or upholds family rights.
entries.studyNote: Distinguish family law in Ruth from prophetic imagery.

entries.name: Rohi
entries.senseAndContext: My shepherd; the LORD pictured as caring and guiding His people.
entries.studyNote: Explore provision and guidance alongside Ezekiel's critique of failed shepherds.

entries.name: Melek
entries.senseAndContext: King; a title for God's sovereign and righteous rule.
entries.studyNote: Connect royal imagery with justice and care.

entries.name: Shofet
entries.senseAndContext: Judge; God judges the earth with righteousness.
entries.studyNote: Judgement is accountable justice, not permission for vengeance.

entries.name: Kadosh Yisrael
entries.senseAndContext: The Holy One of Israel; links holiness with covenant relationship.
entries.studyNote: Trace how holiness and redemption appear together in Isaiah.

entries.name: Tzur
entries.senseAndContext: Rock; poetic image of stability, refuge and faithfulness.
entries.studyNote: Read the metaphor with the surrounding song or prayer.

entries.name: Magen
entries.senseAndContext: Shield; image of God's protection and help.
entries.studyNote: Not a promise that believers will never face harm.

entries.name: Ezer
entries.senseAndContext: Helper; used of God as the one who aids His people.
entries.studyNote: The word does not imply inferiority; compare its use for God and in Genesis 2.

entries.name: Pele Yoetz
entries.senseAndContext: Wonderful Counsellor; part of Isaiah's royal-child titles.
entries.studyNote: Read the oracle's themes of justice, peace and enduring rule.

entries.name: Sar Shalom
entries.senseAndContext: Prince of Peace; a royal title in Isaiah's vision.
entries.studyNote: Study with the promised ruler's character and peace imagery.

entries.name: Abir Yaakov
entries.senseAndContext: Mighty One of Jacob; stresses God's strength toward Jacob's descendants.
entries.studyNote: Observe its use in blessing and restoration poetry.

entries.name: Rishon VaAcharon
entries.senseAndContext: First and Last; declaration of God's sovereignty over history.
entries.studyNote: Read in its polemic against idols and assurance to Israel.

entries.name: Qedem
entries.senseAndContext: Ancient or of old; poetic descriptor of God's everlasting action.
entries.studyNote: Treat as a biblical descriptor, not a separate personal name.

entries.name: El Gibbor
entries.senseAndContext: Mighty God; a title in prophetic and royal contexts.
entries.studyNote: Compare immediate context; avoid isolating the phrase.

entries.name: Rachum
entries.senseAndContext: Compassionate or merciful; description of God's character.
entries.studyNote: Read the full cluster of character descriptions.

entries.name: Chanun
entries.senseAndContext: Gracious; description of God's generous favour.
entries.studyNote: Grace is joined with patience, faithfulness and calls to return.

entries.name: Erekh Appayim
entries.senseAndContext: Slow to anger; phrase describing God's patience.
entries.studyNote: Read patience alongside justice.

entries.name: Rav Chesed
entries.senseAndContext: Abounding in steadfast love; description of covenant mercy.
entries.studyNote: Chesed has a range of relational meanings; avoid one narrow gloss.

entries.name: Emet
entries.senseAndContext: Truth or faithfulness; description of God's reliability.
entries.studyNote: Consider truth as dependable faithfulness.

entries.name: Pater
entries.senseAndContext: Father; relational title used by Jesus and the apostles.
entries.studyNote: Read in prayer, teaching and adoption contexts.

entries.name: Theos
entries.senseAndContext: God; the ordinary Greek designation throughout the New Testament.
entries.studyNote: Let grammar and context guide interpretation.

entries.name: Kyrios
entries.senseAndContext: Lord; title of authority used for God and Jesus.
entries.studyNote: Study how Israel's Scriptures inform New Testament usage.

entries.name: Pantokrator
entries.senseAndContext: Almighty or ruler over all; prominent in Revelation.
entries.studyNote: Read within Revelation's worship and hope amid opposition.

entries.name: Soter
entries.senseAndContext: Saviour; title describing God and Jesus as deliverer.
entries.studyNote: Compare its use across the New Testament.

entries.name: Poimen
entries.senseAndContext: Shepherd; Jesus is the good shepherd who lays down His life.
entries.studyNote: Notice the contrast with those who abandon the flock.

entries.name: Alpha and Omega
entries.senseAndContext: First and last Greek letters; title expressing comprehensive sovereignty.
entries.studyNote: Observe the speaker and context in each occurrence.

entries.name: Logos
entries.senseAndContext: Word; John's prologue describes the one who was with God, was God and became flesh.
entries.studyNote: Read themes of creation, life, revelation and incarnation.

entries.name: Emmanuel
entries.senseAndContext: God with us; Matthew applies Isaiah's sign-language to Jesus.
entries.studyNote: Study Isaiah's historical setting and Matthew's fulfilment reading.

entries.name: Lamb of God
entries.senseAndContext: John the Baptist's designation for Jesus, linked with the removal of sin.
entries.studyNote: Compare Gospel introduction, Revelation imagery and Passover themes.

entries.name: I AM
entries.senseAndContext: A Greek expression used in John's Gospel in sayings revealing Jesus' identity.
entries.studyNote: Read each saying in dialogue; the expression also has ordinary uses.

entries.name: Image of the Invisible God
entries.senseAndContext: Christ makes the invisible God known and is described in relation to creation.
entries.studyNote: Read the whole passage and its claims about creation and reconciliation.

entries.name: Ancient of Days
entries.senseAndContext: Visionary title in Daniel depicting divine authority and judgement.
entries.studyNote: Respect the apocalyptic symbols and distinguish figures in the scene.

entries.name: Most High
entries.senseAndContext: Title emphasising God's supreme authority.
entries.studyNote: Compare contexts across both Testaments.
